description: Composite two-panel figure of mechanical-property data (no micrographs or spectra). Both panels share x = Al content [at%] (2–20, ticks every 2), left y = Strength [MPa] (150–550, ticks every 50) and right y = Strain [%] (labelled ticks 10, 20, 30, 40). (a) is labelled "RT" and (b) "−100 °C". Neither panel carries a symbol legend, so curve identity must follow the caption: filled symbols are tensile yield stress and ultimate tensile strength (left axis), the remaining curves are strain before necking and fracture strain (right axis), and the additional symbol set in (b) is the stress for initiating deformation twinning. In (a) a filled-circle series climbs about linearly from ≈140 MPa at 4 at% Al to ≈440 MPa at 18 at%, paralleled by a dotted open-circle series from ≈250 to ≈500 MPa, while two declining error-barred series (filled down-triangles ≈450→180 in left-axis units, open squares ≈330→180) represent fracture strain and strain before necking. In (b) the strengths are shifted upward (filled circles from ≈210 MPa at 4 at% Al), the strain curves collapse steeply above ≈12 at% Al, and filled up-triangles appear only at ≈14–18 at% Al (≈270–450 MPa). The figure demonstrates linear solid-solution strengthening with concurrent loss of ductility as Al content rises, with deformation twinning accompanying the low-temperature deviation.

observations.observation: Both panels plot several series against Al content [at%] using a shared pair of y-axes: Strength [MPa] (150–550, left) and Strain [%] (right, labelled ticks 10, 20, 30, 40).
Panel (a) is labelled 'RT' in the top-right corner and panel (b) is labelled '−100 °C' in the top-right corner.
In panel (a) the filled-circle series rises monotonically and approximately linearly from ≈140 MPa at 4 at% Al to ≈440 MPa at 18 at% Al with small error bars.
In panel (a) a dotted curve of open circles rises from ≈250 MPa at 4 at% Al to ≈500 MPa at 18 at% Al.

In panel (a) two declining series carry large error bars: filled down-triangles from ≈450 to ≈180 and open squares from ≈330 to ≈180 (left-axis units), the two curves converging at the highest Al contents.
In panel (b) the filled-circle series is displaced upward relative to (a), starting at ≈210 MPa at 4 at% Al and rising to ≈400 MPa near 14 at% Al.
In panel (b) filled upward triangles appear only at Al contents of about 14 at% and above, spanning roughly 270–450 MPa.
Neither panel contains a symbol legend or text identifying which marker denotes which property.

The caption states the plotted quantities are tensile yield stress, ultimate tensile strength, strain before necking and fracture strain, measured at a tension rate of 10^-4 s^-1, with the stress for initiating deformation twinning added in (b).
The caption states the data are for various polycrystalline as-cast Fe-Al alloys of Table 1, at room temperature RT in (a) and at −100 °C in (b), as a function of Al content.
The citing text states that at −100 °C the yield stress and ultimate tensile strength values are higher than at room temperature by about 80 MPa.
The citing text states that deformation twinning was observed at the lower temperature only for higher Al contents, occasionally for 11–14% Al and above 14% Al in all specimens.

The citing text states the fracture strain declines steeply above 15% Al at room temperature and above 12% Al at −100 °C, reaching the strain before necking (brittle fracture without prior necking) at 18% Al at room temperature and above 13% Al at −100 °C.

The citing text states the yield stress increases linearly with Al content up to 18% Al with a hardening coefficient of about 2.2 GPa for these polycrystalline alloys, insensitive to deformation rate and temperature.

The citing text states both strain before necking and fracture strain show apparent relative maxima at about 8 and 12% Al at room temperature, which is less pronounced at −100 °C, and that the data are averages of 3–4 tests differing by at most 3%.

subfigures.description: Room-temperature ('RT' box, top right) plot of strength (left axis, MPa) and strain (right axis, %) versus Al content (2–20 at%). A filled-circle series rises about linearly from ≈140 MPa at 4 at% to ≈440 MPa at 18 at%; a dotted open-circle series rises from ≈250 to ≈500 MPa; a filled down-triangle series with very large error bars declines from ≈450 to ≈180 (left-axis units) and an open-square series with error bars declines from ≈330 to ≈180. Mild humps in the declining curves near 8 and 12 at% Al. No legend inside the panel.

Same axes as (a) but at '−100 °C' (box, top right). Filled circles start at ≈210 MPa at 4 at% Al and rise to ≈400 MPa near 14 at% Al; the dotted open-circle series rises from ≈320 to ≈530 MPa; error-barred filled down-triangles and open squares fall from ≈450 and ≈360 to ≈140–150, with a steep drop above ≈12 at% Al; filled upward triangles (≈270–450 MPa) appear only at ≈14–18 at% Al, which the caption assigns to the stress for initiating deformation twinning.

Magnitudes of the individual error bars are not readable from the plots
